For the League of Nations, see [Member states of the League of Nations](Member_states_of_the_League_of_Nations "Member states of the League of Nations").

The **member states of the United Nations** comprise 193 [sovereign states](Sovereign_state "Sovereign state"). The [United Nations](United_Nations "United Nations") (UN) is the world's largest [intergovernmental organization](International_organization "International organization"). All members have equal representation in the [UN General Assembly](United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly").[[3]](Member_states_of_the_United_Nations#cite_note-3)

The United Nations charter defines the rules for admission of member states. Membership is open to all peace-loving states which accept certain terms of the charter and are able to carry them out. New members must be recommended by the [United Nations Security Council](United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"). In addition to the member states, the UN also invites non-member states to be [observer states](United_Nations_General_Assembly_observers "United Nations General Assembly observers") at the [UN General Assembly](United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly").

## Membership

The criteria for admission of new members to the UN are established in [Chapter II](Chapter_II_of_the_United_Nations_Charter "Chapter II of the United Nations Charter"), Article 4 of the [UN Charter](Charter_of_the_United_Nations "Charter of the United Nations"):[[4]](Member_states_of_the_United_Nations#cite_note-charter_ch2-4)

- Membership in the United Nations is open to all peace-loving states which accept the obligations contained in the present Charter and, in the judgement of the Organization, are able and willing to carry out these obligations.
- The admission of any such state to membership in the [United Nations](United_Nations "United Nations") will be effected by a decision of the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the [Security Council](United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council").


A recommendation for admission from the [Security Council](United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") requires affirmative votes from at least nine of the council's fifteen members, with none of the five [permanent members](Permanent_members_of_the_United_Nations_Security_Council "Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council") using their [veto power](United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power "United Nations Security Council veto power"). The [Security Council](United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council")'s recommendation must then be approved in the [General Assembly](United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly") by a two-thirds majority vote.[[5]](Member_states_of_the_United_Nations#cite_note-5)

In principle, only [sovereign states](Sovereign_state "Sovereign state") can become UN members, and currently, all UN members are sovereign states. Although five members were not sovereign when they joined the UN, they all subsequently became fully independent between 1946 and 1991. Because a state can only be admitted to membership in the UN by the approval of the Security Council and the General Assembly, [a number of states that are considered sovereign](List_of_states_with_limited_recognition "List of states with limited recognition") according to the [Montevideo Convention](Montevideo_Convention "Montevideo Convention") are not members of the UN. This is because the UN does not consider them to possess [sovereignty](Sovereignty "Sovereignty"), mainly due to the lack of [international recognition](Diplomatic_recognition "Diplomatic recognition") or due to opposition from one of the permanent members.

In addition to the member states, the UN also invites non-member states to become [observer states](United_Nations_General_Assembly_observers "United Nations General Assembly observers") at the [UN General Assembly](United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly"),[[6]](Member_states_of_the_United_Nations#cite_note-6) allowing them to participate and speak in General Assembly meetings, but not vote. Observers are generally intergovernmental organizations and international organizations and entities whose statehood or sovereignty is not precisely defined.
